skill.name: relational-database-mcp-cloudbase
skill.description: Guides agents through CloudBase Relational Database operations with MCP tools, including MySQL provisioning, SQL changes, schema initialization, and permission review.
skill.summary: Guides safe CloudBase MySQL management through MCP tools.
skill.author: tencentcloudbase

security_audit.summary: Most static command, filesystem, and blocker findings are false positives caused by Markdown formatting and static documentation references. The hardcoded remote fallback URLs are a confirmed low-risk network concern, and the remote instruction fallback is a medium supply-chain trust concern.

remediation.issue: Remote fallback URLs can load instructions outside the audited package.
remediation.suggestion: Bundle related guidance in the package, or pin fallback URLs to immutable commits and require user confirmation before loading them.

remediation.issue: The skill guides destructive database operations such as destroying MySQL or running DDL.
remediation.suggestion: Require exact environment, table, and action confirmation before destroy, delete, drop, or schema migration steps.

remediation.issue: Permission updates can expose SQL data when applied too broadly.
remediation.suggestion: Use least-privilege permission examples and require queryPermissions verification after every permission update.

content.value_statement: CloudBase MySQL operations need clear tool choice and safety checks. This skill guides agents through MCP-based provisioning, querying, schema changes, and permission reviews.
actual_capabilities: Selects the correct MCP tool for read-only queries, writes, provisioning, and permission changes.
Guides MySQL provisioning and destroy workflows with confirmation and status checks.
Explains safe SQL query, statement, and schema initialization workflows.
Requires _openid on new tables for per-user access control.
Separates MCP database management from SDK-based application development.
limitations: Requires CloudBase MCP tools to be available in the agent environment.
Does not provide SDK code for frontend or backend applications.
Can guide destructive operations, so users must confirm the target environment and action.
References remote fallback documentation for related skills.

use_cases.title: Check Database Readiness
use_cases.description: Confirm whether CloudBase MySQL exists and is ready before any SQL work begins.

use_cases.title: Review Table Permissions
use_cases.description: Inspect and update SQL table permissions after creating or changing schema.

use_cases.title: Run Controlled SQL Maintenance
use_cases.description: Plan read checks, targeted writes, schema initialization, and validation through MCP tools.

prompt_templates.title: Check Database Status
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to check whether CloudBase MySQL is provisioned and ready. Report the status and next safe step.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Safe Read Query
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to inspect a table with a limited read-only query. Summarize the result and avoid write operations.

prompt_templates.title: Initialize a Secure Schema
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to plan schema initialization for CloudBase MySQL. Include _openid where user-scoped access is needed.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Destructive Change
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to plan a destructive database action. Confirm the environment, explain impact, and define validation steps.

output_examples.input: Check if CloudBase MySQL can accept queries.
output_examples.output: Reports whether the instance exists, whether the lifecycle state is ready, and what operation is safe next.

output_examples.input: Create a table for user-owned records.
output_examples.output: Plans schema initialization, includes the per-user access column, and recommends permission verification after creation.

output_examples.input: Destroy the MySQL instance for this environment.
output_examples.output: Requests explicit confirmation, checks the current instance, starts the destroy flow, and polls task status.

best_practices: Confirm environment and table names before writes, schema changes, or destroys.
Run limited read-only queries before mutating data.
Review table permissions after schema creation or permission updates.
anti_patterns: Using SDK setup when MCP tools are available for the management task.
Destroying MySQL without explicit user confirmation and status polling.
Creating user-scoped tables without the _openid access-control column.

faq.question: Does this skill execute database commands by itself?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance for agents that already have CloudBase MCP tools available.

faq.question: Can it build application database code?
faq.answer: No. It is for MCP database management, not SDK-based application development.

faq.question: Which MCP tools does it describe?
faq.answer: It describes queryMysqlDatabase, manageMysqlDatabase, queryPermissions, and managePermissions.

faq.question: Why is _openid important?
faq.answer: The _openid column supports per-user access control for tables with user-owned data.

faq.question: What should happen before destructive operations?
faq.answer: The agent should confirm the target environment, summarize impact, and get explicit user approval.

faq.question: Does it require network access?
faq.answer: The packaged guide does not require network access, but it references remote fallback documentation.
